name: D&D 5th Edition (2014)
description: A GM screen for the 2014 rules: the party's hit points, AC, initiative, passive Perception and spell save DC from the D&D 5e (2014) sheet, an initiative tracker, every condition and exhaustion, setting a DC, skills, cover, light and obscured areas, travel pace and damage by level, plus random tables for NPC names, looks, manners, ideals, bonds and flaws, scene events and quick finds.

sections.title: Blinded
sections.text:
- A blinded creature can't see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.

sections.title: Charmed
sections.text:
- A charmed creature can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects.
- The charmer has advantage on any ability check to interact socially with the creature.

sections.title: Deafened
sections.text: - A deafened creature can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.

sections.title: Exhaustion
sections.text:
Exhaustion is measured in six levels. A creature suffers the effect of its current level as well as all lower levels.

| Level | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Disadvantage on ability checks |
| 2 | Speed halved |
| 3 | Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws |
| 4 | Hit point maximum halved |
| 5 | Speed reduced to 0 |
| 6 | Death |

- If an already exhausted creature suffers another effect that causes exhaustion, its current level increases by the amount specified in the effect's description.
- An effect that removes exhaustion reduces its level as specified, with all exhaustion effects ending if the level is reduced below 1.
- Finishing a long rest reduces a creature's exhaustion level by 1, provided that the creature has also ingested some food and drink.

sections.title: Frightened
sections.text:
- A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.
- The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

sections.title: Grappled
sections.text:
- A grappled creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated.
- The condition also ends if an effect removes the grappled creature from the reach of the grappler or grappling effect, such as when a creature is hurled away by the *thunderwave* spell.

sections.title: Incapacitated
sections.text: - An incapacitated creature can't take actions or reactions.

sections.title: Invisible
sections.text:
- An invisible creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, the creature is heavily obscured. The creature's location can be detected by any noise it makes or any tracks it leaves.
- Attack rolls against the creature have disadvantage, and the creature's attack rolls have advantage.

sections.title: Paralyzed
sections.text:
- A paralyzed creature is incapacitated and can't move or speak.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.

sections.title: Petrified
sections.text:
- A petrified creature is transformed, along with any nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it ceases aging.
- The creature is incapacitated, can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- The creature has resistance to all damage.
- The creature is immune to poison and disease, although a poison or disease already in its system is suspended, not neutralized.

sections.title: Poisoned
sections.text: - A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

sections.title: Prone
sections.text:
- A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.
- The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls.
- An attack roll against the creature has advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature. Otherwise, the attack roll has disadvantage.

sections.title: Restrained
sections.text:
- A restrained creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
- The creature has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

sections.title: Stunned
sections.text:
- A stunned creature is incapacitated, can't move, and can speak only falteringly.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.

sections.title: Unconscious
sections.text:
- An unconscious creature is incapacitated, can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- The creature drops whatever it's holding and falls prone.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.

sections.title: Cover
sections.text:
| Cover | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Half | +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws |
| Three-quarters | +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws |
| Total | Can't be targeted directly by an attack or a spell |

- **Half cover:** an obstacle blocks at least half of the target's body - a low wall, a large piece of furniture, a narrow tree trunk, or a creature, friend or foe.
- **Three-quarters cover:** about three-quarters of the target is covered - a portcullis, an arrow slit, or a thick tree trunk.
- **Total cover:** the target is completely concealed by an obstacle. Some spells can still reach it by including it in an area of effect.
- Behind several sources of cover, only the most protective degree applies.

sections.title: Obscured areas
sections.text:
| Area | Examples | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lightly obscured | Dim light, patchy fog, moderate foliage | Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight |
| Heavily obscured | Darkness, opaque fog, dense foliage | Blocks vision entirely: a creature trying to see something there is effectively blinded |

sections.title: Light
sections.text:
| Light | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Bright | Daylight, torches, lanterns, fires |
| Dim (lightly obscured) | The edge of a light source's reach, twilight and dawn, a bright full moon |
| Darkness (heavily obscured) | Outdoors at night, an unlit dungeon, magical darkness |

| Source | Bright | Dim | Lasts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Candle | 5 ft. | +5 ft. | 1 hour |
| Torch | 20 ft. | +20 ft. | 1 hour |
| Lamp | 15 ft. | +30 ft. | 6 hours a flask of oil |
| Hooded lantern | 30 ft. | +30 ft. | 6 hours a flask of oil |
| Bullseye lantern | 60-ft. cone | +60 ft. | 6 hours a flask of oil |

A hooded lantern with its hood lowered gives dim light in a 5-foot radius. **Darkvision** sees dim light within its range as bright, and darkness as dim, in shades of gray.

sections.title: Travel pace
sections.text:
| Pace | Minute | Hour | Day | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fast | 400 ft. | 4 miles | 30 miles | -5 penalty to passive Wisdom (Perception) scores |
| Normal | 300 ft. | 3 miles | 24 miles | - |
| Slow | 200 ft. | 2 miles | 18 miles | Able to use stealth |

- **Forced march:** past 8 hours of travel in a day, each traveler makes a Constitution saving throw at the end of each extra hour, DC 10 + 1 for each hour past 8. On a failure, they gain one level of exhaustion.
- **Difficult terrain:** travelers move at half speed.

columns.label: Look
entries: Ink-stained fingers
Far too many rings, all of them cheap
A much-mended coat with mismatched patches
Tall, and stoops through every doorway
Spectacles they keep pushing up their nose
Smells of woodsmoke and pipeweed
A faded ship tattooed on one forearm
Odd boots, one noticeably newer
Clothes far too fine for this place
Leans on a cane they don't seem to need
Always nibbling something from a pocket
A tame mouse riding on one shoulder
A ring of keys that jingles with every step
Paint flecks on hands and sleeves
Sunburnt nose and a permanent squint
A wide-brimmed hat they never take off
A holy symbol worn on a bootlace
A freshly bandaged hand
Flour dusted on sleeves and apron
A flower tucked behind one ear

columns.label: Manner
entries: Answers questions with questions
Laughs at their own jokes before the punchline
Leans in to talk, always a little too close
Counts coins while they talk
Calls everyone "friend", enemies included
Never quite finishes a sentence
Has a proverb for every occasion
Sharpens a knife all through the conversation
Stiffly formal and polite
Haggles over everything, even gifts
Talks about themselves by name
Gets every name slightly wrong
Keeps glancing at the door
Brings up a famous cousin at every chance
Holds eye contact a moment too long
Speaks slowly, weighing every word
Interrupts constantly
Superstitious: knocks on wood, spits for luck
Apologises for everything
A little hard of hearing, so shouts

columns.label: Ideal
entries: Family comes before everything
A debt must always be repaid
Knowledge should be free to all
The strong should shield the weak
Tradition keeps the world from falling apart
Coin is the only real safety
Every rule is there to be bent
Beauty is worth any price
The gods are watching; act like it
Freedom, for themselves and everyone
Loyalty to the crown, whoever wears it
Leave every place better than you found it

columns.label: Bond
entries: Owes their life to a stranger they hope to find again
Sends half of every wage to a sibling in the city
Guards a key to a lock they have never seen
Swore an oath at a dying friend's bedside
Keeps a letter they have never dared to send
Protects the village that took them in as a child
Hunts the person who burned their home
Devoted to an old mentor, now frail
Carries a family heirloom everyone else wants
In love with someone far above their station

columns.label: Flaw
entries: Can't keep a secret to save their life
Gambles away anything not nailed down
Lies when the truth would do just as well
Holds a grudge for years
Trusts anyone who flatters them
Goes pale at the sight of blood
Takes credit for other people's work
Drinks to forget, and forgets too much
Hears insults where none were meant
Can't turn down a dare
Hoards things, useful or not
Would sell out a friend for the right price

columns.label: Something happens
entries: A sudden downpour sends everyone looking for shelter
A breathless messenger arrives, looking for someone else
A cart loses a wheel and blocks the way
Someone in the crowd recognises one of the party
A dog runs off with something important
A bell starts ringing in the distance
A fight breaks out nearby
A child asks the party to help find a parent
A merchant offers a deal that seems too good
The lights go out
A stranger slips a note into someone's pocket
The ground trembles, briefly
A patrol arrives asking questions
Smoke rises from a building nearby
A street performer picks one of the party for their act
An animal acts strangely, then bolts
Someone faints
A rival turns up chasing the same goal
Thunder rolls, though the sky is clear
Everyone falls quiet as a procession passes

A pair of loaded dice
A list of names, some crossed out
A stoppered vial that smells of mint
An IOU for a large sum, unsigned
